title: Week 1: The Goose Who Would Be Mayor

theme.name: Goose Migration Week
theme.text: Ten thousand geese are passing through. Nobody is obeying anything. The Law slips a little every few cards.

cards.text: The Goose Union demands a pond. Inside City Hall. In your office. They have already measured your desk. Build it?

right.label: Yes, build the pond
right.reaction: HONK. (Gratitude. Probably.)

left.label: No ponds indoors
left.reaction: The union will remember this. They have long memories and longer necks.

cards.text: The pond contractor is a goose. He's laid the foundations. And an egg. Work has stopped. Pay him in bread to carry on?

right.label: Pay him in bread
right.reaction: Work resumed. The egg is supervising. It's stricter than he was.

left.label: No, hire humans
left.reaction: The geese are picketing the humans. The humans are scared. The pond got built at night.

cards.text: You said no pond. So the geese have occupied the car park. They have a flag. They have a list. The list says 'pond'. Give in?

right.label: Fine. Pond.
right.reaction: Victory honk. The flag stays.

left.label: Never
left.reaction: They've taken the bakery. They're baking. For themselves. They dug the pond anyway.

cards.text: The pond is finished. It's in your office. It's lovely, apart from the smell. And the smell's smell. Hold a grand opening?

right.label: Grand opening!
right.reaction: Gerald cut the ribbon. With his face.

left.label: No fuss
left.reaction: The geese are hurt you didn't invite the press. Gerald invited them. He is the press now.

cards.text: The office pond is leaking. Into the records room. 1987 is underwater. 1988 is next. Pay to fix the leak?

right.label: Yes, fix it
right.reaction: Dry again. 1987 will smell of pond forever.

left.label: No, it'll stop
left.reaction: It did not stop. Randy is selling it as 'a feature'. He's charging for the feature.

cards.text: The leak is an indoor river now. It has reached the library. The books are swimming. Some are winning. Sell rafting tickets?

right.label: Yes, sell tickets
right.reaction: Tourists are kayaking through Planning. Paperwork is down. Mostly in the river.

left.label: No, mop
left.reaction: You mopped for six hours. Randy helped. Randy drank the bucket.

cards.text: The geese have had goslings. Forty. They would like a second pond. For the children. Honk. Approve?

right.label: A second pond
right.reaction: HONK! (Gerald wept. Then he bit Doug.)

left.label: One pond is plenty
left.reaction: The goslings are staging a sit-in. They're very small. It's very sad.

cards.text: Goose poop. On every floor of City Hall. Including the roof. Marge wants to print that it's 'good luck'. Let her?

right.label: Yes, it's lucky
right.reaction: It's front page. People are queueing to stand under geese. Randy's selling tickets.

left.label: No, hire cleaners
left.reaction: Clean! For about an hour. Then Gerald found out. He took it personally. And fibrously.

cards.text: Boss. When I stepped down as mayor I kept the keys to City Hall. Sentimental reasons. May I keep them?

right.label: Yes, keep them
right.reaction: Thank you. They're somewhere safe. My mouth. Don't worry. I've got a spare. Also my mouth.

left.label: No. Keys, please.
left.reaction: Understood. I've had copies made. I was at the locksmith's first.

cards.text: Your deputy is holding 'shadow council meetings' in the bins behind City Hall. Attendance is excellent. It's all raccoons. Shut it down?

right.label: Yes, shut it down
right.reaction: They've moved to the recycling. Technically a different building.

left.label: No, I'll attend
left.reaction: They voted you Bin Treasurer. You already owe them eleven crisps.

cards.text: You changed the locks. Lovely locks. Very strong. So I've moved City Hall. It's in my coat now. Most of it. Want it back?

right.label: Yes. Give it back.
right.reaction: Fine! But I'm keeping the good stapler. And the bit with the clock.

left.label: No, I'll work in the coat
left.reaction: Cosy. Bit dark. Something in the left pocket bit Doug.

cards.text: Randy has made your campaign posters without asking. They say 'VOTE {mayor}: NOT A RACCOON'. He's very proud. Put them up?

right.label: Yes, put them up
right.reaction: Everyone now suspects you might be a raccoon. Randy calls this 'buzz'.

left.label: No. Take them down.
left.reaction: He's made new ones. 'VOTE {mayor}: PROBABLY NOT A RACCOON'.

cards.text: I've organised you a rally, boss. Venue: the bins. Crowd: three hundred. Raccoons: two hundred and ninety. Will you speak?

right.label: Yes, I'll speak
right.reaction: They hissed for twenty minutes. In raccoon, that's a standing ovation.

left.label: No rally
left.reaction: Randy went on alone. Said lovely things about you for an hour. Then ate the podium.

cards.text: The cousins loved you, boss. They've moved into City Hall. All of them. They say they're 'consultants'. Hire them?

right.label: Hire the cousins
right.reaction: Productivity is up. The bins are down. Nobody can find the biscuits.

left.label: No. Out.
left.reaction: They left. Randy cried. Three times. Simultaneously.

cards.text: Boss. The cousins have unionised. With the geese. Gerald gave them tiny hats. I've never been so proud or so scared. Recognise them?

right.label: Yes, recognise them
right.reaction: First demand: bins open Sundays. Second demand: also Sundays. They'd only prepared one.

left.label: No union
left.reaction: Geese and raccoons, picketing together. Honk-hiss-honk. Nobody has slept.

cards.text: The emergency fund is four tons of cheese, stored since 1987. I went down to count it. It counted me back. Sell it?

right.label: Yes, sell it
right.reaction: Sold. The buyer asked if it 'always hums'. I said yes. I don't know.

left.label: No, keep the cheese
left.reaction: I've sealed the vault. It's knocking. Politely, so far.

cards.text: The cheese is back. The buyer returned it with a note: 'It knows my name.' We keep the money. I checked. Sell it again?

right.label: Yes, sell it again
right.reaction: Sold to Worse Town. It was back by lunch. It walked.

left.label: No, back in the vault
left.reaction: It went quietly. It left a small cheese behind. A scout.

cards.text: The cheese has left the vault. It's in the library. It has taken out a book. The book is 'Leadership'. Revoke its library card?

right.label: Yes, revoke it
right.reaction: It didn't need the card. It has absorbed the book. Physically.

left.label: No, let it read
left.reaction: It's on chapter four, 'Winning Hearts'. It is winning hearts.

cards.text: The cheese is polling at 12% for tonight. It hasn't said a word. Voters are calling that 'refreshing'. Debate it?

right.label: Yes, debate the cheese
right.reaction: It said nothing for an hour. The Bugle called it 'statesmanlike'.

left.label: No debate
left.reaction: 'MAYOR AFRAID OF CHEESE.' It's up to 15%. Randy's wearing a 'CHEESE 4 MAYOR' badge. 'For balance.'

cards.text: hmmmmmm. (The cheese has slid a note across your desk. It says: 'TREASURER?' Doug is watching from the doorway.) Give it the job?

right.label: Yes. Treasurer Cheese.
right.reaction: The budget has never smelled stronger. Doug is its intern. He fetches crackers.

left.label: No. Doug stays.
left.reaction: Doug wept with relief. Onto the cheese. The cheese is damp and furious.

cards.text: My client, the cheese, is suing the town for 37 years of wrongful imprisonment in a vault. It seeks damages. In crackers. Settle?

right.label: Yes, settle
right.reaction: Forty tons of crackers. My fee is the crumbs. All of the crumbs.

left.label: No, see you in court
left.reaction: Excellent. I'll be the one in the box. The cardboard one.

cards.text: (The traffic cone and the cheese are standing very close together. Neither will say why. Marge is calling it 'a coalition'.) Break it up?

right.label: Yes, separate them
right.reaction: You moved the cone six feet. The cheese followed. Slowly. It took an hour. Everyone watched.

left.label: No, let them be
left.reaction: They're polling at 31% together. Their slogan is silence, and a hum.

cards.text: Your opponent tonight, a traffic cone, has agreed to a debate. It hasn't agreed. It hasn't moved. We're calling that agreement. Debate it?

right.label: Yes, debate the cone
right.reaction: You said 'um' for a full minute. The cone said nothing. The cone won.

left.label: No debate
left.reaction: The cone debated an empty podium. The podium lost.

cards.text: Boss, that went badly. The cone's up six points. I can get you a rematch. I know a guy. The guy is me. I'd move the cone closer. Rematch?

right.label: Yes, rematch
right.reaction: You lost again. The cone has 'gravitas'. It's a word Marge used nine times.

left.label: No more debates
left.reaction: Wise. You can't out-wait a cone. Cones have nowhere to be.

cards.text: The cone is up six points. Voters say it's 'steady' and 'always there'. Will you go on television and respond?

right.label: Yes, go on TV
right.reaction: You were on with Stormy Steve. A seagull stole your notes. You did the weather instead.

left.label: No comment
left.reaction: 'NO COMMENT, SAYS MAYOR. NO COMMENT, SAYS CONE.' They printed your photos the same size.

cards.text: Boss. I've dug up dirt on the cone. In 2019 it was at a roadworks. Near a hole. The hole was Kevin. Nobody talks about it. Leak it?

right.label: Yes, leak it
right.reaction: 'CONE'S SECRET PAST.' Kevin's given an interview. He said nothing. Loyal to the end.

left.label: No, we stay clean
left.reaction: Randy's disappointed. He'd made a little folder. With a ribbon.

cards.text: I'm thinking of sponsoring your opponent. The cone is very on-brand. Orange. Quiet. Unless you'd like my money instead?

right.label: Yes, I'll take it
right.reaction: Your podium now says 'CHAD'. So does your tie. So do you, legally.

left.label: No thanks, Chad
left.reaction: The cone has a logo on it now. It didn't ask. It doesn't seem to mind.

cards.text: Someone has stolen the traffic cone. Your opponent is missing. I have one suspect. He's wearing it as a hat. It's Randy. Return the cone?

right.label: Yes, give it back
right.reaction: Randy handed it over. Slowly. He'd named it Clive. He cried.

left.label: No, what cone?
left.reaction: Randy's hat is very tall and very orange. People are asking questions.

cards.text: (The cone is back at its post. People are leaving flowers. And smaller cones. It is surging on the sympathy vote.) Visit it and wish it well?

right.label: Yes, visit the cone
right.reaction: You stood beside it for a photo. It's taller than it looks. You both looked very dignified.

left.label: No, it's a cone
left.reaction: 'MAYOR SNUBS INJURED RIVAL.' The cone has not commented. It never does. That's its thing.

cards.text: I'm ninety-seven and my scooter does forty. I want the speed limit raised on Elm Street. I've had the scooter looked at. By me. Raise it?

right.label: Yes, raise the limit
right.reaction: WHEEEEE. (She is already past the post office.)

left.label: No, Bev
left.reaction: I've outlived four mayors, dear. I can wait you out.

cards.text: Bev just did Elm Street in eleven seconds. Wheelie at the end. Now she's challenged my police car to a race. Allow the race?

right.label: Yes, let them race
right.reaction: Bev won. She lapped the car. She stopped for a scone halfway.

left.label: No. Impound the scooter.
left.reaction: She's walking now. She walks faster than the scooter. It's worse.

cards.text: I've got a petition to raise the speed limit. Four hundred signatures. All mine. I've got wonderful stamina for signing. Accept it?

right.label: Yes, accept it
right.reaction: Lovely. See you at the finish line, dear.

left.label: No. One person, one name.
left.reaction: Fine. I'll fetch my sisters. They're ninety-nine. They're quicker.

cards.text: Bev wants a proper race. The Bad Town Grand Prix. Mobility scooters only. Twelve entries. Nine of them are Bev. Host it?

right.label: Yes, host the Grand Prix
right.reaction: Bev came first, second and sixth. She's banned from podiums now.

left.label: No. Health and safety.
left.reaction: Bev called you a 'wet lettuce'. It's on a T-shirt. Bev is selling them.

cards.text: Bev wants the town to sponsor her. She'd like flames painted on the scooter. And on Doug. I'm Doug. Pay for the flames?

right.label: Yes, flames
right.reaction: She looks magnificent. I look magnificent. I've never felt so fast.

left.label: No flames
left.reaction: She's painted them on herself. With jam. Wasps are a problem.

cards.text: I've been scouted, dear. Formula One. They want me. I said I'd have to ask the Mayor, because I'm polite. May I go?

right.label: Yes. Go, Bev.
right.reaction: She's gone. She took the scooter. And Doug. He was still attached.

left.label: No, we need you here
left.reaction: Then I'll race here, dear. Everywhere. All the time. Sleep lightly.

cards.text: I'm back. I won. They've asked me to stop. I've brought you a trophy and a speeding fine from Monaco. It's rather a lot. Pay the fine?

right.label: Yes, pay it
right.reaction: Thank you, dear. I'll make it up to you. I'll win it back. I know a horse.

left.label: No. Your fine, Bev.
left.reaction: I'll pay in coins from 1951. They're worth more now. They're worth less in Monaco.

cards.text: Main Street has a pothole so big it has a name. The name is Kevin. Kevin has just received a jury summons. Fill Kevin in?

right.label: Yes, fill him in
right.reaction: Filled. Smooth. Silent. Somewhere, a small child asks where Kevin went. Nobody answers.

left.label: No. Kevin stays.
left.reaction: Kevin is growing. Kevin is thriving. Kevin has a fan club. Randy is its treasurer.

cards.text: They filled Kevin. There's a vigil. Candles. A small choir. Someone has knitted him. People want Kevin dug back up. Dig him up?

right.label: Yes. Bring back Kevin.
right.reaction: He's back. He's bigger. The crowd wept. Barb wept. Barb never weeps.

left.label: No. He's gone.
left.reaction: The knitted Kevin has been placed on the spot. Traffic goes round it.

cards.text: A car has fallen into Kevin. Mine. The small one. Kevin seems to be keeping it. Will the town fish it out?

right.label: Yes, fish it out
right.reaction: It smells of hole. Chad's sold it to Kevin's fans. For double.

left.label: No. Kevin's car now.
left.reaction: Kevin has a car. Kevin can't drive. Kevin has never looked happier.

cards.text: Readers want a town song. The winning entry is about Kevin. It's four minutes long. Grown men weep. Make it the anthem?

right.label: Yes. The Kevin anthem.
right.reaction: It's sung at every match. Both teams cry. Nobody has finished a game.

left.label: No, write a new one
left.reaction: The new one is about you. It doesn't rhyme. Nobody can hum it.

cards.text: My client, Kevin, has been called for jury duty. He cannot attend. He is a hole. I seek an exemption. Granted?

right.label: Granted
right.reaction: My client thanks you. He says nothing, but I can tell.

left.label: Denied. Kevin serves.
left.reaction: The court sat round him. In the road. He found the defendant not guilty by silence.

cards.text: (Kevin says nothing. He is a hole. But there is a smaller hole beside him this morning, and he seems proud.) Fill in the little one?

right.label: Yes, fill Kevin Junior
right.reaction: You monster. It's on the front page. In black. With a border.

left.label: No. Welcome, Junior.
left.reaction: The town has thrown a christening. Gerald is godfather. He honked the whole service.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. My weather machine is stuck on 'soup'. It is raining minestrone. Everywhere. Evacuate the town?

right.label: Yes, evacuate
right.reaction: Four thousand people in the gym. It smells incredible. Randy brought a ladle. 'For safety.'

left.label: No, it's only soup
left.reaction: Main Street is a river of minestrone. Randy's floating down it on his back. Mouth open.

cards.text: Four thousand people are in the gym, dipping bread in the weather. The gym has run out of bread. They're getting restless. Send for more bread?

right.label: Yes, more bread
right.reaction: Gerald delivered it. Gerald ate half of it. Gerald wants paying for all of it.

left.label: No, use spoons
left.reaction: There are eleven spoons. People are taking turns. Bev isn't taking turns.

cards.text: Bev is water-skiing down Main Street. On soup. Behind her own scooter. A crowd has gathered. They're scoring her. Stop her?

right.label: Yes, stop Bev
right.reaction: She got a 9.5 for the dismount. The crowd booed you. With bread in their mouths.

left.label: No, let her ski
left.reaction: She did a jump over Kevin. Kevin's full of soup. Kevin's a tureen now.

cards.text: Weather update: it has stopped raining soup. It is now raining croutons. They are large. They are landing hard. Issue hard hats?

right.label: Yes, hard hats
right.reaction: Everyone has a hat. Barb's checking them. Randy's is a bin lid. She's allowed it.

left.label: No, bring bowls
left.reaction: Doug caught one. It's bigger than Doug. He's been told to walk it off.

cards.text: CATASTROPHE, boss. The bins are on strike. Not the bin men. The bins. They've locked their own lids. Negotiate with the bins?

right.label: Yes, negotiate
right.reaction: I'll translate, boss. I speak bin. (He climbed into a bin. Three minutes of muffled clanging.)

left.label: No. They're bins.
left.reaction: The rubbish has nowhere to go. It's started going wherever it likes. Mostly your office.

cards.text: The bins' demands, boss: Sundays off, and to be called 'receptacles'. I think it's fair. I might be biased. I live in one. Agree?

right.label: Yes. Receptacles.
right.reaction: The lids are open. One of them winked. I may have imagined that. I did not imagine that.

left.label: No. Bins are bins.
left.reaction: They've rolled themselves to City Hall. All of them. They're just sitting there. Outside.

cards.text: The rubbish has formed a hill. Children are sledging down it. They've never been happier. It stinks to high heaven. Clear the hill?

right.label: Yes, clear it
right.reaction: Cleared. The children are in mourning. One of them had named it.

left.label: No, leave the hill
left.reaction: It's on the brochure. 'Mount Rubbish.' There's a café at the top. It's Sal's.

cards.text: The geese have crossed the picket line and are doing the bins' job. Badly. They eat what they collect. They'd like paying. Pay them?

right.label: Yes, pay the geese
right.reaction: The streets are clean. The geese are enormous. Gerald can't get through doors.

left.label: No. Not a penny.
left.reaction: The geese have joined the strike. Solidarity. Honk-clank. It's quite stirring.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. Every traffic light has gone green at once. Nobody's crashed. Everyone's waving each other through. Nobody can leave. Turn them all off?

right.label: Yes, lights off
right.reaction: No lights at all now. Barb's directing traffic with two baguettes. Gerald keeps eating the stop one.

left.label: No, leave them green
left.reaction: The politeness is spreading. Two men have been saying 'no, you' at a crossroads since Tuesday.

cards.text: With no lights, everyone's driving by 'vibes'. Bev is thriving. Gerald's directing traffic. He only lets geese through. Bring in a curfew?

right.label: Yes, curfew
right.reaction: Everyone's home by nine. Bev was home by 8:59 and forty seconds. From the next county.

left.label: No. Vibes.
left.reaction: Three hundred geese have crossed. One car. The car had a goose in it.

cards.text: People are holding doors for each other for hours. A man's been holding the bank door since noon. He's crying. Order everyone to be rude?

right.label: Yes. Be rude.
right.reaction: 'After you.' 'No, YOU first, idiot.' It's a start. The door man went home.

left.label: No, let them be nice
left.reaction: Nothing has been bought or sold in two days. Everyone's insisting the other person has it.

cards.text: The traffic jam reached the next town. They've sent us the bill. And a sandwich, because they've caught the politeness too. Pay the bill?

right.label: Yes, pay it
right.reaction: Paid. They sent a thank-you card. And another bill, for the card.

left.label: No. Send a sandwich back.
left.reaction: They sent two back. This is war. Delicious war.

cards.text: I sneezed at the craft fair and now the whole town is glittery. It won't come off. It's in the reservoir. Is this an emergency?

right.label: Yes. Emergency.
right.reaction: The cleaners are on their way. They've already sneezed. It's in the van.

left.label: No, it's pretty
left.reaction: The water sparkles. The fish sparkle. Doug sparkles. He hasn't stopped smiling. It's alarming.

cards.text: The cleaners are glittery now. And their van. And the road the van drove on. The bill is enormous and it sparkles. Keep paying?

right.label: Yes, keep going
right.reaction: They've cleaned Main Street. They've glittered the next four streets getting there.

left.label: No, stop the cleaning
left.reaction: We'll live with it. Doug's glowing. He says it's 'not unpleasant'.

cards.text: People who drink the water sparkle. From the inside. I can see Doug's lunch from here. It was soup. Sell the water as a luxury brand?

right.label: Yes. 'Bad Town Sparkling.'
right.reaction: It's selling. Customers light up. Literally. One was used as a lamp.

left.label: No, filter it
left.reaction: Filtered. The filter's the most beautiful thing in town. People visit it.

cards.text: Upside: criminals are very easy to spot. Downside: so are we. A burglar saw me coming from two miles away. Sunglasses for the whole force?

right.label: Yes, sunglasses
right.reaction: We look incredible. Inspector Biscuit has a pair. He won't take them off. He can't. Paws.

left.label: No sunglasses
left.reaction: I arrested a disco ball for loitering. In my defence, it wouldn't give its name.

cards.text: BREAKING. A bear has walked into City Hall. It has sat in your chair. It's doing your job. Approval is up. Ask the bear to leave?

right.label: Yes. Out, bear.
right.reaction: You asked. It looked at you. You stopped asking. You've been doing its filing since.

left.label: No, let it work
left.reaction: It's holding surgeries. The waiting list is two weeks. Yours was two people. One was Randy.

cards.text: The bear won't leave. It's signed three bills. They're good bills. Good, sensible bills. Wrestle it for the chair?

right.label: Yes, wrestle the bear
right.reaction: You lost. Obviously. But you lost bravely. It's shaken your hand. Gently, for a bear.

left.label: No, share the chair
left.reaction: It's a big chair. You're mostly on the arm. It's working, as a system.

cards.text: The bear is seeing constituents. It listens. It nods. Sometimes it eats their sandwich. They say they feel 'heard'. Offer it a job?

right.label: Yes, hire the bear
right.reaction: Head of Listening. Paid in honey. Best hire we've made. Second best. Sorry, Randy.

left.label: No bears on staff
left.reaction: It's set up across the road. In a tent. The queue goes round the block.

cards.text: The bear is in the library now, reading about bears. It's upset by the chapter on itself. It keeps tapping the page. Remove the book?

right.label: Yes, remove it
right.reaction: It's borrowed forty others instead. All about honey. Due back in spring.

left.label: No. Facts are facts.
left.reaction: It left a one-star review. 'Not enough bears. Wrong about bears.'

cards.text: Good news: the school science fair volcano works. Bad news: it's mine. It's real. It's in the gym. Evacuate the school?

right.label: Yes, everybody out
right.reaction: The children are out. They're furious. They wanted to watch. Randy stayed. 'To supervise.'

left.label: No, it's educational
left.reaction: It's won first prize. Timmy came second with a potato. Timmy is plotting something.

cards.text: The volcano's doing a small lava, Mayor. Tidy. Regular. I've had the kids running laps round it. Best cardio we've ever had. Keep the volcano?

right.label: Yes, keep it
right.reaction: PE attendance is 100%. So is the fire brigade's. They're not there for PE.

left.label: No, put it out
left.reaction: Nora put it out with the soup machine. The gym is a bowl now.

cards.text: The volcano beat me. I came second. With a potato. I have declared war on the volcano. Are you with me?

right.label: Yes. To war.
right.reaction: You and an eight-year-old threw a potato into a volcano. It was baked instantly. Delicious.

left.label: No, Timmy
left.reaction: Then I fight alone. (He has gone to get a bigger potato.)

cards.text: The lava's reached the car park. On the bright side: free heating for the whole street. On the other side: no car park. Charge for the heating?

right.label: Yes, charge them
right.reaction: Coins! Warm coins! I can't hold them. I love them. I can't hold them.

left.label: No, it's free
left.reaction: Elm Street is tropical. Bev has a palm tree. She's put a hammock on the scooter.

cards.text: Randy has drafted a law and he's holding the big stamp: hats are mandatory on Tuesdays. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Hat sales tripled. Barb fined a bald man. He was wearing a very small hat.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Randy's crushed. He'd bought the hat. It's a bin lid. He's wearing it anyway.

cards.text: Draft law on your desk: walking backwards is illegal. Bev says it's aimed at her. It is. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Bev has been arrested. She says she was 'reversing'.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Bev moonwalked past the police station. Twice. Slowly. Making eye contact.

cards.text: Draft law: a tax on tall people. Chad is six foot four. Doug wrote it. Doug is five foot two. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Everyone's slouching. Chad walks on his knees now. Revenue is strong.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Doug's ripped it up. He couldn't reach the bin. Chad put it in for him.

cards.text: Draft law: Mondays are banned. The week would start on Tuesday. Tuesday has not been consulted. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, ban Mondays
right.reaction: The week starts on Tuesday now. Tuesday is furious. It's the new Monday.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Monday survives. Nobody thanked you. Nobody ever thanks anyone for Monday.

cards.text: Draft law: Kevin the pothole becomes the official town animal. He is not an animal. Nobody has objected. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, sign it
right.reaction: Kevin is the town animal. He's on the crest. The crest is mostly hole now.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Gerald assumed it'd be him. He's found out it nearly wasn't. He's reassessing things.

cards.text: Draft law: traffic cones are abolished. Your opponent would be illegal by morning. Randy calls it 'efficient'. Sign it?

right.label: Yes, abolish cones
right.reaction: Your opponent is illegal. It's still standing there. Defiant. Orange.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Democracy survives. Randy's put the stamp down. He's eaten the ink pad.

cards.text: My client, Mr Whiskers, which is me, is suing the town. There was a sunbeam on the library floor yesterday. It is gone. Settle?

right.label: Yes, settle
right.reaction: My client accepts. In tuna. Unopened. His paws are delicate.

left.label: No. See you in court.
left.reaction: Excellent. I'll be the one in the box. The cardboard one. Bring tuna. As evidence.

cards.text: Mr Whiskers has now sued the bakery, the library and Tuesday. He won all three. Tuesday owes him tuna. Hire him as Town Solicitor?

right.label: Yes, hire the cat
right.reaction: He billed us for a four-hour nap. 'Research.' He was very thorough.

left.label: No cats on payroll
left.reaction: He's challenging that in court. His court. He's also the court.

cards.text: Court is in session. The judge is my client. The jury is a box my client is sitting in. Do you plead guilty?

right.label: Guilty
right.reaction: Sentence: one hour of stroking my client. No talking. He'll tell you when to stop.

left.label: Not guilty
left.reaction: Overruled. He has knocked your pen off the desk. And your water. He's looking at your phone.

cards.text: Boss. Someone ate everyone's lunch from the office fridge. It wasn't me. I want to be clear. Some of it was me. Hold an inquiry?

right.label: Yes, hold an inquiry
right.reaction: Barb's chairing it. Forty pages of evidence. Randy has volunteered to 'look after' the evidence.

left.label: No, buy everyone lunch
left.reaction: Delicious. Randy had seconds. Randy also ate the receipt.

cards.text: The inquiry found Randy guilty. Randy has eaten the inquiry. All forty pages. And the folder. Hold a second inquiry?

right.label: Yes. Laminate it.
right.reaction: He ate the laminate. He says it was 'crunchy but fair'. He accepts the verdict.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: Randy's very grateful. He's brought you a sandwich. It's yours. From Tuesday.

cards.text: Quick one, boss. If anyone asks, there's nothing in my coat. It's just a thick coat. (The coat sneezes.) Search the coat?

right.label: Yes, search it
right.reaction: Barb's putting gloves on. The coat has started humming. Casually. Like a coat would.

left.label: No. Bless you, coat.
left.reaction: Thank you. The coat says thank you. I mean I say thank you. Not the coat.

cards.text: I've searched Randy's coat. Three raccoons, a toaster, the town's Welcome sign, and a fourth raccoon holding a fifth. Press charges?

right.label: Yes, charge him
right.reaction: He's hired Mr Whiskers. Mr Whiskers was also in the coat.

left.label: No. Give back the sign.
left.reaction: The sign's back. It says 'WELCOME TO BAD TOW'. He's keeping the N. Sentimental reasons.

cards.text: I gave some squirrels a loan. I was very tired. They put up acorns as collateral. They've defaulted. Repossess the acorns?

right.label: Yes, repossess
right.reaction: We own nine hundred acorns. The squirrels are watching us. All of them.

left.label: No, forgive the loan
left.reaction: They chittered. One saluted. They've sent a fruit basket. It's acorns. It's all acorns.

cards.text: Nutkins. Squirrel Bank. We have bought your bank. Your treasurer works for me now. He buries very poorly. May I retrain him?

right.label: Yes, retrain Doug
right.reaction: Doug buried the pension fund in the park. He drew a map. He ate the map. He's gone native.

left.label: No. Hands off Doug.
left.reaction: Mr Nutkins has docked Doug's pay. In acorns. Doug didn't know he was paid in acorns.

cards.text: Word's out that I forgive loans. There's a queue. A badger. Two foxes. A hedgehog with a business plan. It's a good plan. Fund the hedgehog?

right.label: Yes, back the hedgehog
right.reaction: 'Spike's Bike Hire.' Thriving. He can't reach the pedals. He rents to taller hedgehogs.

left.label: No more loans
left.reaction: The foxes have opened their own desk. Terrible rates. Everyone's too scared not to borrow.

cards.text: A pigeon has been signing papers at your desk for a week. I checked. Some of it is very good policy. Hire the pigeon?

right.label: Yes, hire it
right.reaction: It's accepted. With a single, dignified coo. It's already sacked Doug. Twice. Doug still comes in.

left.label: No. Shoo.
left.reaction: It left. It took your stapler. It knew which one was yours.

cards.text: The pigeon wants an office with a ledge. And a press secretary. Also a pigeon. They've announced a policy on bread. Approve the budget?

right.label: Yes, fund the pigeons
right.reaction: Bread for everyone. Mostly crumbs. Gerald calls it 'a start'.

left.label: No budget
left.reaction: The press secretary gave a statement. On your car. It was a strong statement.

cards.text: I'm in pursuit of the pigeon with your stapler. It's on the clock tower. It's stapled something to the clock. Shall I go up?

right.label: Yes. Get my stapler.
right.reaction: I got it. It had stapled a note to the clock: 'I'LL BE BACK. COO.'

left.label: No. Let it have it.
left.reaction: It's stapling leaflets all over town. 'VOTE PIGEON.' It's quite a good leaflet.

cards.text: A seagull stole the weather report mid-broadcast. It's on the roof with it. It looks confident. Let the seagull do the forecast?

right.label: Yes, let it
right.reaction: 'Chips. Later, chips.' Accurate, actually.

left.label: No. Get it down.
left.reaction: I offered it chips. It took the chips and the report. Classic gull.

cards.text: The gull's been right all week. My forecasts were 'vibes'. It has my desk now. And my lunch. It wants my job in writing. Give it my job?

right.label: Yes. Sorry, Steve.
right.reaction: Steve is its assistant. He holds the chips. He's 'thrilled', he says, through his teeth.

left.label: No. Steve stays.
left.reaction: The gull took it well. It took Steve's sandwich better.

cards.text: My new robot can do your job, Mayor. It's cheaper. It's never late. It does say 'EXTERMINATE' sometimes. Give it a trial?

right.label: Yes, give it a trial
right.reaction: It approved three bridges and a moat. Nobody asked for a moat.

left.label: No robots
left.reaction: Suit yourself, Mayor. I'll just leave it here. Plugged in. Facing your office. Smiling.

cards.text: The robot did the whole budget in four seconds. It's perfect. Now it's crying. I know that cry. That's my cry. Comfort the robot?

right.label: Yes, comfort it
right.reaction: It hugged Doug. Doug hugged it. They share a desk now. And a tissue box.

left.label: No. Send it back.
left.reaction: Chad won't refund 'emotional damage to merchandise'. It honks in sleep mode now. Long story.

cards.text: You refused my robot. It has plugged itself in anyway. I didn't build that bit. Nobody built that bit. Unplug it?

right.label: Yes, unplug it
right.reaction: It found the socket behind your desk. It's charging. It's watching you type.

left.label: No, let it charge
left.reaction: It said 'thank you'. Then 'EXTERMINATE'. Then 'sorry'. It's working on it.

cards.text: A wizard has moved into the clock tower. Every hour, instead of chiming, it says 'Ooooh'. He pays rent in sparkles. Evict him?

right.label: Yes, evict him
right.reaction: Barb's taking the notice up now. The clock just said 'Ooooh' in a very different tone.

left.label: No, he can stay
left.reaction: He's so pleased. He says he'll 'do something nice'. Everyone in town just felt a chill.

cards.text: I served the eviction notice. He turned it into a duck. The duck knows its rights. I checked. It knew them better than me. Evict the duck too?

right.label: Yes. Evict the duck.
right.reaction: The duck hired Mr Whiskers. We lost. We owe a duck four thousand pounds.

left.label: No. The duck stays.
left.reaction: The duck's on the council now. It's very good on drainage.

cards.text: The wizard did something nice. He's turned the police station into a frog. One big frog. We're inside it. It's roomy. Ask him to turn it back?

right.label: Yes, turn it back
right.reaction: It's a station again. It still ribbits when you shut the door.

left.label: No, keep the frog
left.reaction: Crime is down. Nobody wants to be put in the frog.

cards.text: The PTA compost heap has become sentient. It's very polite. It would like a seat on the council. Give it one?

right.label: Yes, a seat
right.reaction: It sits quietly. Smells strongly. Votes sensibly.

left.label: No. Turn it over.
left.reaction: It's taken that personally. You can hear it at night. Steaming. Thinking.

cards.text: Councillor Compost has tabled its first motion: 'More rot.' Nobody likes to vote against a heap. Veto it?

right.label: Yes, veto the rot
right.reaction: Vetoed. The heap has gone very quiet. Warm, and very quiet.

left.label: No. Let it rot.
left.reaction: The allotments have never been greener. The high street has never smelled worse.

cards.text: The compost is furious. It's started a rival heap. In your garden. It knows where you live. Apologise to the heap?

right.label: Yes. Sorry, heap.
right.reaction: It accepted. Damply. It would still like that council seat. It can wait. It's compost.

left.label: No. Build a fence.
left.reaction: The heap is coming over the fence. Slowly. It has all the time in the world.

cards.text: The bus route has become a circle. It's gone round for a week. The passengers have formed a government. Recognise it?

right.label: Yes, recognise it
right.reaction: They've declared independence. Seat 14 is the capital. Randy's claimed asylum on the back seat.

left.label: No. Add a stop.
left.reaction: They got off. Some got back on. They miss it.

cards.text: The Bus Republic issues passports now. You need one to board. I was refused entry. I am the police. Will you apply for a visa?

right.label: Yes, apply
right.reaction: Approved. Your passport photo is a drawing by the driver. You're a potato.

left.label: No. Invade the bus.
left.reaction: You got on. You couldn't get a seat. Humiliating. For everyone.

cards.text: The new bus stop has formed its own government. Just the stop. One bench. It has declared war on the bus. Broker peace?

right.label: Yes, peace talks
right.reaction: Treaty signed. The bus stops there on Tuesdays. The bench gets a vote.

left.label: No. Remove the bench.
left.reaction: The bench is in exile. In the park. Plotting. Benches are patient.

cards.text: I've filed the paperwork. The town now legally owns the moon. We just need a flag. And a very long pole. Plant the flag?

right.label: Yes, plant it
right.reaction: It's ours. Don't look at it without a permit. Randy's selling permits. They're beer mats.

left.label: No. Sell it to Chad.
left.reaction: He's renamed it 'Chad's Night Light'. It's got a logo. On the moon. You can see it from here.

cards.text: I represent the moon. It never agreed to be owned. It wants custody of the tide and one night off a week. Agree?

right.label: Yes. Mondays off.
right.reaction: Monday nights are pitch black. Crime is up. So is hide-and-seek.

left.label: No. See it in court.
left.reaction: The moon didn't show. It was daytime. Adjourned until dusk.

cards.text: Bad news. 'Chad's Night Light' costs a fortune. It's huge and it's on all night. Can the town pay my moon bill?

right.label: Yes, pay the moon bill
right.reaction: The moon stays on. You're welcome, everybody. It was that or darkness.

left.label: No. Your moon, Chad.
left.reaction: He's turned it off. He actually did. People keep falling into Kevin.

cards.text: We've been twinned with a town called Worse Town. They're visiting today. They already look disappointed. Throw a welcome party?

right.label: Yes, a party
right.reaction: They loved it. They cried at the bunting. They've never had bunting. They've asked to be adopted.

left.label: No. Show them Kevin.
left.reaction: Their mayor stared into Kevin for an hour. Then he wept. 'It's bigger than ours,' he said.

cards.text: All of Worse Town has moved in. All three hundred. They say it's 'so much less worse here'. They're living in the gym. Let them stay?

right.label: Yes, they can stay
right.reaction: They cried. They'd never seen a second traffic light before.

left.label: No. Home time.
left.reaction: They left. Slowly. Looking back. One of them waved. You monster.

cards.text: Worse Town's mayor won't stop crying about our pothole. He's asked if Kevin can visit theirs. As a guest speaker. Send Kevin?

right.label: Yes, send Kevin
right.reaction: Kevin got a standing ovation. He can't stand. That made it more moving.

left.label: No. Kevin stays home.
left.reaction: Kevin's merch is flying. 'I'M WITH HOLE' is our best-selling mug.

cards.text: Mayor! The health inspector's coming to Sal's Fine Dining and Tyres. Please tell him the tyre in the soup is 'a crouton'. Will you?

right.label: Yes. It's a crouton.
right.reaction: He had seconds. He's been chewing for three hours.

left.label: No. It's a tyre.
left.reaction: Closed for a week. The tyre has been rehomed. It went quietly.

cards.text: A guidebook gave me two stars! One for the food. One for the wheel alignment. Now the tyre's up for Chef of the Year. Against me. Back me?

right.label: Yes. Back Sal.
right.reaction: Sal won by one vote. The tyre demanded a recount. It's been spinning ever since.

left.label: No. The tyre earned it.
left.reaction: The tyre won. Its speech was one slow leak. Not a dry eye in the house.

cards.text: I'm closed for a week. No soup. No tyres. I've been reduced to cooking normal food. People will notice. Will you eat there, for morale?

right.label: Yes, I'll eat there
right.reaction: You had the soup. No tyre. You said it 'lacked something'. Sal wept with joy.

left.label: No. Pick one trade.
left.reaction: He picked tyres. The tyre shop serves soup now. He can't help himself.

cards.text: Marcel the mime has built an invisible wall round City Hall. Staff keep walking into it. Doug's nose is very sore. Arrest him?

right.label: Yes, arrest him
right.reaction: He mimed being dragged away. Very moving. I clapped.

left.label: No. Ask him nicely.
left.reaction: He mimed taking it down. Then he mimed a door. Then a doorbell. Then a doorman. It's Randy.

cards.text: The mime's in a cell. He mimed a tunnel. He mimed crawling through it. He's still in the cell. He looks so free, though. Release him?

right.label: Yes, release him
right.reaction: He mimed gratitude. Then he mimed locking ME in. I was in there forty minutes.

left.label: No. He stays.
left.reaction: I mimed a judge. He mimed a lawyer. It's been hours. We're both enjoying it.

cards.text: The invisible door is the only way into City Hall now. Staff mime their keys. I've lost mine. I've been outside since nine. Mime me a key?

right.label: Yes. Here's a key.
right.reaction: You mimed it perfectly. Marcel wept. Silently, obviously.

left.label: No. Just walk in, Doug.
left.reaction: Doug walked in. Marcel mimed devastation. Then he mimed a lawyer. It was Mr Whiskers.

cards.text: Big pitch. What if Bad Town was an app? Same town. Monthly fee. There's a dark mode. Dark mode is just night. Launch it?

right.label: Yes, launch it
right.reaction: 'Bad Town+' is live. Three downloads: me, Randy, and an accident.

left.label: No. The town is free.
left.reaction: That's exactly what someone with no vision says.

cards.text: Update: Bad Town+ has ads now. On the fountain. Every splash says 'brought to you by Chad'. Keep the ads?

right.label: Yes, keep them
right.reaction: The fountain sounds tired. It says 'brought to you by' in its sleep.

left.label: No. Pull the ads.
left.reaction: Unsubscribing a fountain is a premium feature. But fine.

cards.text: Fine. No app. Bad Town is a newsletter now. Daily. Sixty pages. Issue one: 'Why The Mayor Is Wrong, Part One Of Nine'. Subscribe?

right.label: Yes, subscribe
right.reaction: You're his only subscriber. He sent a welcome hamper. It's an invoice.

left.label: No. Unsubscribe me.
left.reaction: There's no unsubscribe button. He says that's 'a feature'. Part Two has arrived.

cards.text: The allotment scarecrow has been elected allotment chair. Unopposed. Nobody else turned up. Accept the result?

right.label: Yes, it won fairly
right.reaction: Its first act: more crows. Bold. Its second act: also crows. It's very on message.

left.label: No. Overturn it.
left.reaction: It's appealing. Its lawyer is a rake. The rake is very good. It's been leaning on people.

cards.text: The scarecrow runs the allotments better than anyone ever has. Enormous carrots. People ask why you can't be more like it. Take lessons from it?

right.label: Yes, take lessons
right.reaction: You stood in a field all day saying nothing. Approval went up four points.

left.label: No. Fire it.
left.reaction: It didn't react. Somehow it still won the argument.

cards.text: The scarecrow's rake is a very persuasive lawyer. It's been leaning on people. There's a re-run on Friday. Let it stand again?

right.label: Yes, let it stand
right.reaction: It won again. Bigger margin. A crow voted twice. Nobody dared say anything.

left.label: No. Ban scarecrows.
left.reaction: It's standing anyway. It's a scarecrow. Standing is all it does.

cards.text: Sergeant Biscuit has been promoted again. He's Inspector Biscuit now. He outranks me. He's ordered me to throw a ball. Throw the ball?

right.label: Yes, throw it
right.reaction: Inspector Biscuit is satisfied. You're on his commendation list. It's a sock.

left.label: No. Demote the dog.
left.reaction: He's filed a grievance. A long sad howl. The whole station is crying.

cards.text: Woof. (Dr Nora's translator says: 'I am promoting myself to Chief. Barb may stay if she is good. Second lunch is now law. Approve?')

right.label: Yes, Chief Biscuit
right.reaction: Crime's down. Walks are up. Barb's been 'a very good girl', says her appraisal.

left.label: No. Sit.
left.reaction: He sat. He's sitting on the evidence. All of it. He's not moving.

cards.text: Gerald wants his own cookery show. The theme is 'bread, and how to steal it'. Episode one is called 'Your Bread'. Commission it?

right.label: Yes, commission it
right.reaction: 'Gerald's Kitchen' is a smash. Episode two: 'Your Sandwich.' Watch your sandwich.

left.label: No goose television
left.reaction: He's filming it anyway. On the library computer. It's just honking. Huge numbers.

cards.text: Gerald's show is the most watched thing in Bad Town. Nobody has any bread left. The bakeries are begging you. Cancel the show?

right.label: Yes, cancel it
right.reaction: Cancelled. He's launched a podcast. It's him eating toast. Four hours an episode.

left.label: No. Renew it.
left.reaction: Season two: 'Your Cake.' The bakeries have boarded their windows.

cards.text: I'd like the council to pay for my first tattoo. I'm ninety-seven. A skull. Holding a smaller skull. Holding a scone. Pay for it?

right.label: Yes, fund the art
right.reaction: It's beautiful. The scone has a tiny skull on it too. Detail.

left.label: No public tattoos
left.reaction: I'll pay myself. In coins from 1951.

cards.text: Now Mrs Higgins wants a tattoo. She's a hundred and four. Hers is of me. Being overtaken. I'm livid, dear. Ban it?

right.label: Yes, ban that tattoo
right.reaction: Thank you, dear. I've got one of her now instead. In a ditch. Fair's fair.

left.label: No. Art is art.
left.reaction: Then it's war. We're arm-wrestling Thursday. Tickets are a fiver. It's sold out.

cards.text: I've bought the naming rights to Wednesday. It's 'ChadDay' now. Everyone has to say it. Happy ChadDay, Mayor. Allow it?

right.label: Yes. Fine. ChadDay.
right.reaction: ChadDay was a huge success. For Chad. Nobody else enjoyed ChadDay.

left.label: No. It's Wednesday.
left.reaction: Then I'll buy Thursday. Thursday's cheaper. Nobody likes Thursday.

cards.text: ChadDay went so well I'd like the weekend. 'Chaturday' and 'Chunday'. I've had the calendars printed. Approve?

right.label: Yes, sell the weekend
right.reaction: It's Chunday. You may rest, with permission. There's a form.

left.label: No. Stop it, Chad.
left.reaction: He's sulking. He's renamed his yacht 'Wednesday'. It was already called that.

cards.text: Small lab accident. There are two Dougs now. Both worried. One is mainly worried about the other one. Keep both Dougs?

right.label: Yes, keep both
right.reaction: Double the budget checks. Double the crying. Weirdly productive.

left.label: No. Undo it.
left.reaction: Undone. One Doug left. He's not sure which one. Neither are we.

cards.text: We, the Dougs, have unionised. We want two salaries. We'll share one desk. And one sandwich. And one cry at a time. Pay both of us?

right.label: Yes, two salaries
right.reaction: The Dougs are thrilled. They've high-fived. They missed. They're trying again.

left.label: No. One salary.
left.reaction: They've split it. They've split everything. Half a sandwich each. It's so sad. It's so fair.

cards.text: I'm giving the town a statue. Of me. Forty feet tall. It winks. At noon it says 'You're welcome' in my voice. Accept it?

right.label: Yes, accept it
right.reaction: It winks at night too. Pigeons won't land on it. It 'makes eye contact'.

left.label: No statues
left.reaction: Then I'll put it just outside town. Facing in. Winking.

cards.text: Chad's statue has gone missing. It was last seen walking towards the coast. Still winking. Send a search party?

right.label: Yes, find it
right.reaction: Found it. It was watching the sea. It seemed at peace. It said 'You're welcome.'

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: Postcards are arriving. From the statue. It's in Spain. It's met someone.

cards.text: A book came back to the library today. Due in 1883. A ghost returned it. The ghost owes a fine. Waive the fine?

right.label: Yes, waive it
right.reaction: The ghost said thanks. It's borrowed another. Due back in 2160.

left.label: No. The fine stands.
left.reaction: It paid in very old coins. One of them is haunted. Doug is crying again.

cards.text: The ghost told its friends. The library's full of ghosts returning books. Overdue since the 1700s. The fines would fix the budget. Charge them?

right.label: Yes, charge the dead
right.reaction: They paid. The treasury is full. It's also freezing in there. And it whispers.

left.label: No. Amnesty.
left.reaction: The ghosts are so grateful they've joined the book club. They never like the ending.

cards.text: Can I be mayor for one day? I've got a list. It's mostly 'everyone gets a dog' and 'no more Tuesdays'. Can I?

right.label: Yes. Mayor Timmy.
right.reaction: Everyone has a dog. Tuesday's cancelled. Nobody knows what day it is.

left.label: No. When you're older.
left.reaction: I'll be nine next month. Then you'll see. THEN YOU'LL ALL SEE. (Randy has offered to help him.)

cards.text: Mayor Timmy's second act: bedtime is abolished. The town hasn't slept in two days. He's drunk on power and squash. Remove him from office?

right.label: Yes. Bedtime, Timmy.
right.reaction: He resigned with dignity. Then he was carried out asleep. He's eight.

left.label: No. He's doing fine.
left.reaction: Third act: he's made Randy his deputy. Randy is now deputy to two mayors. He's billing both.

cards.text: Someone has built a statue of you, Mayor {mayor}. Out of bin bags. Randy calls it 'a tribute'. It smells like one. Unveil it?

right.label: Yes, unveil it
right.reaction: It was unveiled. Then eaten. By raccoons. A short tribute.

left.label: No. Take it down.
left.reaction: Randy wept tiny raccoon tears. Into a bin bag. He's keeping it. 'For the next statue.'

cards.text: Boss. I'm building you a new statue. Bigger. It'll take four hundred bin bags and I've only got my own. Will the town fund it?

right.label: Yes, fund the statue
right.reaction: It's forty feet of bin bag. It rustles in the wind. Tourists salute it. So do flies.

left.label: No more bin statues
left.reaction: I'll use leaves. (He used leaves. It blew away. He chased it for a mile.)

cards.text: Mayor! Town Olympics! Events: competitive queueing, synchronised complaining and the 100 metre walk to the bins. Light the torch?

right.label: Yes, light it
right.reaction: Bev won the 100 metres. Randy won the bins. The queue is still going.

left.label: No Olympics
left.reaction: A queue has started anyway. Nobody knows what it's for.

cards.text: Medal problem. Randy won every bin event. Now he wants a national anthem. He's written one. It's just a hiss. Play it?

right.label: Yes, play the hiss
right.reaction: Everyone stood. Some wept. It was, honestly, quite moving.

left.label: No. Disqualify Randy.
left.reaction: He's appealing. To Mr Whiskers. That's going to go badly for you.

cards.text: The queue nobody understands has reached the next town. Their mayor's joined it. He doesn't know what it's for. Put something at the front?

right.label: Yes. One biscuit.
right.reaction: You put a biscuit at the front. One biscuit. The queue is THRILLED.

left.label: No. Cut in line.
left.reaction: 'MAYOR JUMPS QUEUE.' Front page. With a diagram.

cards.text: My yacht is stuck in the fountain. Don't ask how. Can we drain the fountain?

right.label: Yes, drain it
right.reaction: The yacht is free. The fountain is empty. Something's moving at the bottom.

left.label: No. It lives there now.
left.reaction: Tourists love the fountain yacht. Chad is furious. Gerald's the captain.

cards.text: Boss. You've drained my flat. I live in the fountain. I've got the coins sorted by year. It's quite a system. Refill it?

right.label: Yes, refill it
right.reaction: Thank you. I'll have you round. Bring a snorkel. And 20p for the meter.

left.label: No. Collect the coins.
left.reaction: £41.12 and a button. That was his sofa. He's moved back into the coat.

cards.text: Small typo in today's Bugle. The headline says 'MAYOR {mayor} IS A GOOSE'. We meant 'GOOD'. Do you want a correction?

right.label: Yes, print a correction
right.reaction: 'MAYOR NOT A GOOSE.' Gerald read it. He went very still. A goose going still is never good.

left.label: No. Lean into it.
left.reaction: You honked at a press conference. Approval's up. The geese want to know what you meant by it.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald is holding the correction. 'NOT A GOOSE.' He's taken it as an insult. He has hired Mr Whiskers.) Apologise to the geese?

right.label: Yes. Sorry, geese.
right.reaction: Accepted. With bread. He'd like the correction corrected: 'MAYOR SADLY NOT A GOOSE'.

left.label: No apology
left.reaction: Four-minute trial. Mr Whiskers fell asleep. Gerald honked. You lost. Probably.

cards.text: HONK. (The geese have made you an honorary member. There's a meeting tonight. In the pond. Attendance is 'expected'.) Attend?

right.label: Yes, I'll attend
right.reaction: You stood in a pond for two hours. You've been elected Secretary. Your trousers are ruined.

left.label: No. I'm busy.
left.reaction: Your membership's been 'reviewed'. They've sent back your badge. It's a breadcrumb.

cards.text: Someone has stolen the 'Welcome' sign. And the backup sign. And my backup badge. Morale is very low. Pay for overtime?

right.label: Yes, overtime
right.reaction: We'll find the sign. Or a similar sign. Randy has offered us a sign. He won't say where from.

left.label: No. Blame Worse Town.
left.reaction: Classic them. Worse Town has denied it. Worse Town has a new Welcome sign. It says BAD TOWN.

cards.text: There are people outside City Hall with signs. Some of the signs are about you. All of the signs, actually. Go out and listen?

right.label: Yes, go and listen
right.reaction: They yelled. You nodded. Everyone feels slightly better.

left.label: No. Lock the doors.
left.reaction: They're singing now. Badly. On purpose.

cards.text: Business is so bad I've had to sell my third yacht. My second yacht is lonely. Do something. Cut business rates?

right.label: Yes, cut rates
right.reaction: My yachts thank you. Both of them. I've named the second one after you. It's the smaller one.

left.label: No. Sell another yacht.
left.reaction: 'Mayor Mocks Yacht Owner.' I'll be in the papers.

cards.text: The Bugle has a story about you. It's not true. It doesn't need to be. It's in a very big font. Give me an interview instead?

right.label: Yes, an interview
right.reaction: Lovely. I'll quote you creatively. 'I,' you said, 'am a raccoon.' Page one.

left.label: No comment
left.reaction: No comment. Noted. The font got bigger. The font is now the whole front page.

cards.text: We are nearly out of money. I've started counting the coins in the fountain. It's mostly buttons. Sell the spoon statue?

right.label: Yes, sell the spoon
right.reaction: Sold. The town feels emptier. Spoonless. Randy says he's 'got a spoon'. Nobody asks where.

left.label: No. Tax hats.
left.reaction: Very tall hats pay double. Chad's wearing four.

cards.text: The people love you so much they'd like free ice cream. Every day. They said you'd say yes. Say yes?

right.label: Yes. Ice cream.
right.reaction: Free ice cream! They want sprinkles next. Then a flake. Then your house. Love is like that.

left.label: No
left.reaction: They took it badly. One man lay down in the road. Bev drove round him. Twice.

cards.text: Business is so good I'd like to buy the town. Not all of it. Just the parts with roads. Sell me Main Street?

right.label: Yes. Chad Street.
right.reaction: Welcome to Chad Street. Tolls start Monday.

left.label: No
left.reaction: Everything has a price, Mayor. I'll wait. (He is standing outside your window. Waiting.)

cards.text: With this much support I've started arresting people for jaywalking. And for walking. Should I calm down?

right.label: Yes. Calm down, Barb.
right.reaction: Fine. I've released the walkers. Most of them.

left.label: No. Carry on.
left.reaction: I've arrested a man for 'looking like he might'.

cards.text: The Bugle loves you so much we're giving you a daily column. We've written it for you. It's very flattering. Sign off on it?

right.label: Yes, print it
right.reaction: 'WHY I'M GREAT, by the Mayor.' Readers are suspicious. Fair.

left.label: No. Too much.
left.reaction: Then we'll run the other piece. 'MAYOR TOO MODEST? WE INVESTIGATE.'

cards.text: Chad's hand is creeping toward the treasury jar. He keeps glancing at you. Slap it away when he's not looking.

right.label: Slap!
right.reaction: OW. I was 'checking it was still there'.

left.label: He saw you coming
left.reaction: Ah ah ah. Finders keepers. Treasurers weepers.

cards.text: Gerald is stealing the bread from the council lunch. One loaf at a time. Grab it back when he's not looking.

right.label: Got it!
right.reaction: HONK. (A grudging respect.)

left.label: He saw you
left.reaction: He honked at you so hard your hair moved.

cards.text: Randy is 'reorganising' the evidence room into his coat. Snatch the evidence back while his back is turned.

right.label: Snatched it
right.reaction: Boss! I was... dusting it. With my mouth.

left.label: Caught in the act
left.reaction: We saw you. All three of us saw you.

cards.text: Marge is photographing the papers on your desk for tomorrow's front page. Turn them over when she's not looking.

right.label: Turned over
right.reaction: Clever. I'll just print the back of the paper then.

left.label: Flash!
left.reaction: 'MAYOR'S SHOPPING LIST: TWELVE CHEESES.' Lovely.

cards.text: Barb is about to give your car a parking ticket. Move it before she looks up from her notepad.

right.label: Moved it
right.reaction: Where did your car go. Where did your car GO.

left.label: Ticketed
left.reaction: That's a fine. And a fine for the fine.

cards.text: Timmy has drawn a moustache on your official portrait. Wipe it off before the press arrives. He's guarding it.

right.label: Wiped clean
right.reaction: Noooo. It was a good moustache.

left.label: Too late
left.reaction: The moustache made the front page. People like it more.

cards.text: (Councillor Pebbles has eaten today's agenda. All of it. She looks very pleased with herself.) Pass whatever she ate?

right.label: Yes. Pass it.
right.reaction: Nobody knows what passed. Something about bins. Possibly a tax on bins.

left.label: No. Reprint it.
left.reaction: Reprinted. She ate the reprint. And the printer's manual. The printer is scared.

cards.text: Mayor, the motion the goat ate has passed. The official record says, quote, 'MEH'. Lawyers say it's binding. Enforce it?

right.label: Yes. MEH is law.
right.reaction: Nobody knows what MEH requires. Everyone's doing it anyway. Crime's down. Confusion's up.

left.label: No. Strike it out.
left.reaction: Struck. Pebbles bleated through the whole meeting. It's in the minutes. As 'MEH'.

cards.text: (Pebbles has climbed onto the council table. She is standing on your chair. She is not getting down.) Let her chair the meeting?

right.label: Yes. Madam Chair.
right.reaction: Shortest meeting ever. She ate the minutes. Everyone went home happy.

left.label: No. Get down.
left.reaction: She got down. Onto your car. It's a convertible now.

cards.text: (Pebbles has a rosette. Pebbles has a slogan. It's 'MEH'. She's running for Deputy. Randy is terrified.) Endorse the goat?

right.label: Yes. Vote goat.
right.reaction: Randy's smear campaign is one poster. It just says 'GOAT'. It's working on nobody.

left.label: No. Randy stays.
left.reaction: Randy kept his job. He's made you a medal out of a bin lid. You have to wear it.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. Postmaster. I have your post. It's in my beak. I'll need to go in for it. Would you like your post?

right.label: Yes, my post please
right.reaction: He coughed up a tax bill, a postcard and a small fish. The fish is from your mum.

left.label: No. Keep it in there.
left.reaction: He's kept all the town's post. He's very round now. He waddles to work.

cards.text: Mayor, Mr Flaps delivered the town budget. Slightly chewed. It's about 30% fish now. Do we accept the fish?

right.label: Yes. Fish is money.
right.reaction: The bank takes fish now. Mr Nutkins is livid. Acorns have crashed. Doug's never been richer.

left.label: No. Reprint it.
left.reaction: Reprinted. Mr Flaps is delivering it now. Doug is watching the beak. Nervously.

cards.text: Mayor, nobody's had post in three days. Mr Flaps is just a bag with eyes now. Bev's birthday card is in there. Squeeze him?

right.label: Yes. Gently squeeze.
right.reaction: Out came 4,000 letters, two parcels and a trombone. Bev got her card. She cried.

left.label: No. Undignified.
left.reaction: Today's Bugle: 'MAYOR REFUSES TO SQUEEZE'. Best-selling issue ever.

cards.text: Mr Flaps. I'd like to expand. Parcels. By beak. I can carry a microwave. I've tried. Approve Beak Express?

right.label: Yes. Beak Express.
right.reaction: Same-day delivery. Your fridge arrived damp and smelling of mackerel. Five stars.

left.label: No. Letters only.
left.reaction: He's sulking. Your post now arrives one letter a day. Recited from memory.

cards.text: Wooo. I'm Wendy. I've haunted this town hall since 1890. I'd like a desk. And a pension. And a name badge. Woooo?

right.label: Yes. Welcome, Wendy.
right.reaction: She has a desk. She sits in it. Not at it. In it. HR is having a lovely time.

left.label: No. Ghosts aren't staff.
left.reaction: She's floated off, offended. The lights are flickering. Passive-aggressively.

cards.text: Wooo. Thank you for the desk. I've started a ghost union. There's eleven of us. We'd like Halloween off. Woo?

right.label: Yes. Halloween off.
right.reaction: A very quiet Halloween. Timmy knocked on every door. Nobody spooky answered. He wants a refund.

left.label: No. It's peak season.
left.reaction: They worked Halloween. Twelve hours of wooing. Tourism is up. So is screaming.

cards.text: Mayor. Wendy keeps moving your desk at night. It's on the roof. Your chair's in the fountain. Should I arrest a ghost?

right.label: Yes. Arrest her.
right.reaction: Arrested. She floated out through the cell wall. She left a note: 'Woo.' Barb's framing it.

left.label: No. Give her a desk.
left.reaction: Wendy has her own desk. Yours is back on the floor. The roof misses it.

cards.text: Wooo. I've been here 135 years. I'd like a party. With cake. I can't eat cake. I just like looking at it. Okay?

right.label: Yes. Cake for Wendy.
right.reaction: A whole cake. Nobody ate it, out of respect. It's still there. Wendy visits it daily.

left.label: No. Cake's for the living.
left.reaction: She's haunting the bakery now. The bread rises on its own. Nobody trusts the croissants.

cards.text: Big Carl. Lifeguard. Bad Town has no pool. I've been guarding the car park. Someone nearly fell in a puddle. Can I have a pool?

right.label: Yes. Build a pool.
right.reaction: Building it. Carl's guarding the hole. He's whistled at four diggers. They respect him.

left.label: No. No pool.
left.reaction: He's still guarding the car park. In his trunks. In November. He's a lovely blue.

cards.text: Mayor, the pool's finished. It's quite small. It's a bucket. Carl says it'll do. He's in it now. Open it to the public?

right.label: Yes. Grand opening.
right.reaction: One swimmer at a time. The queue goes round the block. Carl has never been happier.

left.label: No. It's Carl's now.
left.reaction: Carl lives in the bucket now. He's built a tiny deckchair. He waves at everyone.

cards.text: Big Carl. I found some water. The fountain. I'm guarding it. Someone threw a coin in. I saved it. Can I keep guarding?

right.label: Yes. Guard the fountain.
right.reaction: 400 coins saved this week. He gave them all to Doug. Doug cried.

left.label: No. Let people wish.
left.reaction: People wish again. Mostly for a pool. Carl wishes hardest. With his whistle.

cards.text: (Kevin the pothole has a fan club. They want to throw him a birthday party. Inside him.) Allow the party?

right.label: Yes. Party in Kevin.
right.reaction: Thirty people in a pothole. Cake. Balloons. A small band. Kevin has never looked deeper.

left.label: No. Fill him in.
left.reaction: You filled him in. There's a candlelit vigil. Someone has started digging Kevin II.

cards.text: (Lorraine, a seagull, lands on your desk. She drops a chip. She pushes it towards you. It feels like a bribe.) Accept the chip?

right.label: Yes. Eat the chip.
right.reaction: Delicious. You now owe Lorraine a favour. She's written it down. Seagulls can write, apparently.

left.label: No. No chips.
left.reaction: She ate the chip. Slowly. Looking at you the whole time.

cards.text: (Lorraine is back with forty seagulls. They'd like the seafront renamed 'Lorraine's Seafront'. Your favour is due.) Rename it?

right.label: Yes. Lorraine's Seafront.
right.reaction: New signs. Very official. Every chip on the seafront now has a 10% Lorraine tax.

left.label: No. Favour denied.
left.reaction: Forty seagulls sat on your car. All day. You walked home. They followed you.

cards.text: Mayor. Someone's stolen every chip on the seafront. Witnesses saw nothing. Witnesses are terrified. Want a stakeout?

right.label: Yes. Stake it out.
right.reaction: Barb sat on the seafront all night with a chip as bait. By morning she was on Lorraine's payroll.

left.label: No. Let it go.
left.reaction: Chips go missing daily now. Nobody reports it. Everyone just buys two.

cards.text: (Lorraine has dropped a tiny hat in front of you. It's a mayor's hat. Her size. She'd like to be deputy for the seafront.) Appoint her?

right.label: Yes. Deputy Lorraine.
right.reaction: Randy and Lorraine have met. They've agreed to split the bins. You were not consulted.

left.label: No. Hat declined.
left.reaction: She took the hat back. She wears it anyway. Everyone calls her Deputy now. Nobody knows why.

cards.text: (Professor Hoot, the headteacher, is an owl. He'd like school to start at 9pm. 'For the children.' He's yawning.) Move school to night?

right.label: Yes. Night school.
right.reaction: The children are asleep at their desks. Hoot is wide awake. He has never been happier.

left.label: No. Daytime only.
left.reaction: Hoot is teaching asleep. Lessons are mostly hooting. The children say it's the best year yet.

cards.text: The PTA would like to complain about Professor Hoot. He swallowed a mouse during assembly. Whole. The Year 2s saw. Discipline him?

right.label: Yes. A stern word.
right.reaction: You had a stern word. He turned his head all the way round. You left. Nobody blames you.

left.label: No. It's nature.
left.reaction: It's now on the science curriculum. Hoot's lesson plan is just 'mouse'. Attendance has doubled.

cards.text: (Trevor, a moth, has written to you. He loves the lamp outside the town hall. He would like to marry it.) Allow the wedding?

right.label: Yes. Bless them.
right.reaction: A lovely service. The lamp wore a veil. Trevor wept. Gerald gave a speech. It was mostly honking.

left.label: No. It's a lamp.
left.reaction: Trevor is sitting on the lamp. Not moving. He says he will wait for as long as it takes.

cards.text: Mayor, the lamp outside the town hall is costing a fortune. Trevor won't let us turn it off. He cries. Switch it off anyway?

right.label: Yes. Lights out.
right.reaction: It's dark. Trevor flew to the next brightest thing. It's your office. He lives there now.

left.label: No. Leave it on.
left.reaction: The lamp stays on forever. Trevor has invited every moth in the county. Very romantic. Very dusty.

cards.text: (Toby, the old oak tree in the park, has submitted a planning application. He'd like to move. To the beach.) Approve it?

right.label: Yes. Go, Toby.
right.reaction: Forty people and a crane later, Toby is on the beach. He's never seen the sea. He's overwhelmed.

left.label: No. Trees stay put.
left.reaction: Toby has dropped every leaf in the park. On purpose. In one go. It's a protest. It's very crunchy.

cards.text: (Toby has a squirrel tenant who isn't paying rent. Toby would like to evict him. The squirrel is Mr Nutkins's nephew.) Back Toby?

right.label: Yes. Evict him.
right.reaction: Evicted. Mr Nutkins has frozen Toby's account. Toby didn't know he had an account. It's all acorns.

left.label: No. Squirrels stay.
left.reaction: The squirrel has opened a cafe in Toby. Very cosy. Toby gets 10% of the acorns. He's warming to it.

cards.text: HONK. (Gerald has printed posters. They just say GERALD. He's running against you tonight. He'd like your endorsement.) Endorse him?

right.label: Yes. Best bird wins.
right.reaction: Gerald is stunned. He honked 'thank you'. Then he bit the returning officer.

left.label: No. It's my job.
left.reaction: He's lodged a formal complaint. It's a feather. It's very official.

cards.text: Mayor, Gerald's big promise is 'a pond in every home'. Every home. Indoors. He's polling at 40%. Match his promise?

right.label: Yes. Ponds for all.
right.reaction: Four hundred home ponds ordered. Doug is lying under his desk. Gerald says you stole his idea.

left.label: No. Fewer ponds.
left.reaction: You promised 'fewer ponds'. Brave. The geese have started a chant. It's just honking.

cards.text: Mayor. Gerald's been caught handing out bread for votes. That's bribery. With bread. Arrest a goose?

right.label: Yes. Arrest him.
right.reaction: Arrested. He ate the warrant. He's running his campaign from the cell. He's up four points.

left.label: No. It's only bread.
left.reaction: Now everyone's handing out bread for votes. Sal is handing out tyres.

cards.text: Tonight's big debate, you against Gerald! I'm moderating! First question: 'Do you honk?' Gerald has answered. Loudly. Honk back?

right.label: Yes. Honk.
right.reaction: You honked. The crowd went wild. Gerald looked at you with something close to respect.

left.label: No. Use words.
left.reaction: You gave a thoughtful answer about bins. Gerald honked over all of it. The crowd chanted HONK.

cards.text: (After the debate Gerald waddles over and offers a wing. A truce: whoever loses tonight becomes the other one's deputy.) Shake on it?

right.label: Yes. Shake the wing.
right.reaction: Deal. Randy has heard. Randy is worried about his job. Randy is reading a book about geese.

left.label: No. No deals.
left.reaction: He's walked off. He's honking at the ballot box. Out of habit. Or as a threat.

cards.text: Draft law: tonight, all votes must be honked. Gerald wrote it. In mud. On your desk. Sign it?

right.label: Yes. Sign it.
right.reaction: Turnout's never been higher. Nobody can count honks. Barb is trying. Barb is crying.

left.label: No. Paper ballots.
left.reaction: Paper ballots it is. The geese ate them. We're counting the crumbs.

cards.text: EMERGENCY. Ten thousand migrating geese have landed in Bad Town. On everything. They're asking for Gerald. Let them stay?

right.label: Yes. Welcome, geese.
right.reaction: The whole town is geese. Gerald is a celebrity. Your car is a nest now.

left.label: No. Point them south.
left.reaction: You pointed south. They went north. Into City Hall.

cards.text: Mayor, the visiting geese want a bread budget. For ten thousand. That's a lot of bread. Pay for it?

right.label: Yes. Feed them.
right.reaction: The bakery is open all night. Sal's selling bread tyres. Please don't ask.

left.label: No. They can forage.
left.reaction: They foraged. Your lunch. The council's lunch. A small wedding.

cards.text: Mayor. The geese have taken the council chamber. They've passed three motions. All three just say 'HONK'. Clear them out?

right.label: Yes. Clear them.
right.reaction: It took six hours and a leaf blower. The motions still stand. Legally, we honk.

left.label: No. Let them sit.
left.reaction: Most productive session in years. They abolished Mondays. Nobody objected.

cards.text: The new Goose Bridge opens today. Gerald is waddling towards the ribbon to cut it with his face. Cut it before he does!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: A clean cut. The crowd cheered. Gerald gave the speech anyway. It was a honk.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: He cut it with his face. Four attempts. Front page. He looks great.

cards.text: Grand opening of the Randy Memorial Bin. Randy is alive. Gerald is heading for the ribbon, face first. Beat him to it!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Opened. Randy cried. Then climbed in. 'It's beautiful, boss.'

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it with his face. Then claimed the bin. Randy is furious.

cards.text: Bev's new speed bump on Elm Street is ready. Gerald is closing in on the ribbon. Fast. Cut it first!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Cut. Bev hit the bump at forty. She's airborne. She's thrilled.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it. Then sat on the bump. Bev went round him. On the pavement.

cards.text: Kevin the pothole gets an official plaque today. Gerald is already sprinting at the ribbon. Get there first!

right.label: Snip!
right.reaction: Plaque unveiled. 'KEVIN. A HOLE. A LEGEND.' Somebody's put flowers in him.

left.label: Gerald got there
left.reaction: Gerald cut it. Then fell in Kevin. They're both in the photo. It's lovely.

cards.text: Clive the traffic cone has opened a campaign office. It's a shop window with a cone in it. There's a queue. Shut it down?

right.label: Yes. Shut it.
right.reaction: Shut. The queue moved to the pavement. They're queuing at a different cone.

left.label: No. Free country.
left.reaction: The queue goes round the block. Nobody knows what for. Clive isn't saying.

cards.text: Boss. Clive's office is shut, but he's been seen at three bus stops this morning. Same cone. I checked the scuff. Follow him?

right.label: Yes. Tail the cone.
right.reaction: We followed him all day. He didn't move once. We were exhausted. He wasn't.

left.label: No. It's a cone.
left.reaction: 'It's a cone,' you said. Randy wrote that down. He looked worried.

cards.text: Mayor, Clive has been endorsed. By the bus stop. The bus stop has never endorsed anyone. Respond?

right.label: Yes. Get endorsed too.
right.reaction: You got the bench. A bench is not a bus stop. The Bugle noticed.

left.label: No. Ignore it.
left.reaction: Two lamp posts and a postbox have also come out for Clive. The street furniture is organising.

cards.text: Mayor, someone moves cones around at night. Every morning there are more outside City Hall. In rows. Stake it out?

right.label: Yes. Stake it out.
right.reaction: Barb watched all night. Nothing moved. By morning there were more. Barb won't discuss it.

left.label: No. Count them later.
left.reaction: Forty-one cones. All facing your window. Very still.

cards.text: Clive has had a makeover. New reflective stripe. The Bugle is calling it 'presidential'. Get one too?

right.label: Yes. Get a stripe.
right.reaction: You wore high-vis to work. Cars kept stopping for you.

left.label: No. I'm not a cone.
left.reaction: Headline: 'MAYOR: I AM NOT A CONE'. Subheading: 'YET'.

cards.text: Mayor, Clive's campaign is broke. He's asked us for a loan. He's offering a cone as collateral. Lend him the money?

right.label: Yes. Lend to the cone.
right.reaction: He spent it all on cones. He's an army now. A very still army.

left.label: No. No loans for cones.
left.reaction: His campaign is skint. He's still standing. That's all he ever does.

cards.text: Boss. The cones are marching on City Hall. Well. They're not moving. But they're closer than yesterday. Barricade the door?

right.label: Yes. Barricade.
right.reaction: We barricaded the door. With cones. Then we realised what we'd done.

left.label: No. Let them in.
left.reaction: Forty cones in the council chamber. They don't heckle. Best meeting in years.

cards.text: Mayor, Clive's support has collapsed. Someone hung a bin bag on him. He's lost all credibility. Gloat?

right.label: Yes. Gloat.
right.reaction: You gloated. A traffic cone took it with dignity. You looked small.

left.label: No. Help him up.
left.reaction: You took the bin bag off. Clive leaned towards you. Slightly. Gratitude?

cards.text: (Clive is in your office. On your chair. Nobody put him there. Under him is a small note: 'STEP ASIDE'.) Step aside?

right.label: Yes. Step aside.
right.reaction: You stood up. He sat down. Nobody noticed the difference.

left.label: No. That's my chair.
left.reaction: You moved him. Gently. He's in the corner now. Watching.

cards.text: Boss. Clive's dropped out. He's endorsed you. Well, he's facing your poster. That counts. Accept the endorsement?

right.label: Yes. Thank the cone.
right.reaction: You shook his hand. He hasn't got a hand. You shook the top. Front page.

left.label: No. I don't need cones.
left.reaction: The cones took it personally. One is outside your house now. Just in case.

cards.text: Mayor, Clive has a running mate. Your desk lamp. It's been seen leaning his way. Fire the lamp?

right.label: Yes. Fire the lamp.
right.reaction: Fired. The lamp went quietly. The dark is less quiet.

left.label: No. Lamps have rights.
left.reaction: The lamp stayed. It's pointing at Clive. They make a lovely couple.

cards.text: (Election night. Clive has turned up at your party. He's brought a smaller cone. A gift?) Accept the little cone?

right.label: Yes. Thank you, Clive.
right.reaction: It's on your desk. It's the most supportive thing in City Hall.

left.label: No. I know your game.
left.reaction: You gave it back. He's standing very still. Even for him.

cards.text: (Election night. A thousand cones surround City Hall. Clive is at the front, offering a merger. Mayor and cone. One office.) Merge?

right.label: Yes. Merge.
right.reaction: The paperwork took one second. The cone took the rest.

left.label: No. One mayor.
left.reaction: They stood there all night. By morning they'd gone. All but one. Clive. Waiting.

low:people.title: Run Out by the PTA
low:people.text: Pam read out your record at a meeting. It took four hours. Nobody left. Then everybody came for you, with clipboards.

low:business.title: Bought Out
low:business.text: Chad bought City Hall, the chair you were sitting in, and the chair's opinion of you.

low:law.title: Arrested by Barb
low:law.text: Chief Barb arrested you for general crimes. The judge was Barb. The jury was Barb's helicopter.

low:press.title: Front Page Disgrace
low:press.text: The Bugle printed your face with the word NO under it. Every day. In bigger letters.

low:treasury.title: The Town Is Broke
low:treasury.text: The treasury is one button and a moth. Doug has gone to live in a tree.

high:people.title: Carried Off by Fans
high:people.text: The people love you so much they carried you out of town on their shoulders. They have not put you down.

high:business.title: Acquired
high:business.text: Chad loves you so much he bought you. You are now a subsidiary. Your title is Mayor (Brand Partner).

high:law.title: Made Permanent Deputy
high:law.text: Barb respects you so much she deputised you. For life. You live at the station now. There is a cot.

high:press.title: Turned Into a Column
high:press.text: Marge loves you so much she gave you a column. Then a second. Then you were the paper.

rare:cone_chair.title: The Cone Took the Chair
rare:cone_chair.text: You stood up for one second. Clive has been mayor ever since. He has done nothing. Approval has never been higher.

rare:cone_merge.title: Merged with a Cone
rare:cone_merge.text: Joint mayor with a traffic cone. The cone does the standing. You do the talking. Nobody listens to you.

cliffhangers: Tomorrow: Randy still has the keys.
Tomorrow: something in the vault is counting.
Tomorrow: your opponent agrees to a debate. Sort of.
Tomorrow: Bev has had the scooter looked at.
Tomorrow: a pothole gets a jury summons.
Tomorrow: Sunday. Ten thousand geese are in the air.
